title: AI Clinical Trials Have a Consent Crisis: 58% of Forms Fail to Explain AI's Role
source_used: TrialSite News (lead paragraphs from the page's excerpt)
key_facts: Hankun Su and Fen Xiao, co-first authors at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, China, led the study 'Informed Consent Disclosures and Minimum Requirements in AI Clinical Trials: Cross-Sectional Analysis'.
It was published on 2 Jul 2026 in the Journal of Medical Internet Research.
The study examined 114 AI-related clinical trials.
58% of consent forms failed to disclose AI's type or purpose; 18.4% omitted risk disclosures; only 14% met the study's combined readability and length standards.
Su revisited the findings in a commentary on 14 Oct 2026, warning that traditional informed consent may be inadequate for AI-driven research.
quote_evidence: Examining 114 AI-related clinical trials, researchers found 58% of consent forms failed to disclose AI's type or purpose, 18.4% omitted risk disclosures, and only 14% met the study's combined readability and length standards.
Su revisited these findings in an October 14 commentary, warning that traditional informed consent may be inadequate for AI-driven research.
why_it_matters_hint: Patients joining AI trials may not be told what AI does in their care.
